newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian business invite mid-sized western firms.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian business invite mid-sized western firms.

text.p: Hungary's Industrialists Association (GYOSZ) aims to attract more medium-sized western companies to the country, mainly to support multinationals already present, GYOSZ said on Friday.
"We recently signed an agreement with the German Industrialists' Association to this effect," Gabor Szeles, President of GYOSZ, told a news conference.
He added that as a concrete step the two associations will link their databases to facilitate exchange of business information.
Szeles also said that multinationals with an established presence in Hungary not only need subcontractors, but are also looking at other, so far relatively overlooked markets.
"Projects are underway which, with the help of GYOSZ, would assist multinationals to establish presence in neighbouring countries," he said.
One of the areas GYOSZ is looking at is the Transylvania region of Romania, Szeles said.
"Some of the projects are in an advanced stage, but I cannot say more at the moment," he added.
Hungary has attracted over $13 billion of foreign direct investment so far, including Germans who account for 25 percent.
